pr_title: tests: fix these tests when using EFI console output function as default
pr_body:
This PR try to fix some testcases when applying the UEFI console as default output （with UART_CONSOLE disable)

Category 1: Implemented the simplest driver to support EFI console:
- Add a minimal EFI console driver to support printf, fix following tests: 
tests/benchmarks/sys_kernel/ 
samples/application_development/external_lib/  
samples/posix/eventfd/
samples/userspace/hello_world_user/

- Implement a logging backend EFI console to fix following tests:  
samples/subsys/logging/syst
tests/subsys/logging/log_core_additional/
samples/subsys/logging/logger/

Category 2:  And there is a firmware bug that EFI console output call return with interrupt enabled. Though
there is a interrupt disabled solution that disable the interrupt right after EFI call, in some case
it the interrupt could happen during the EFI call context. If an interrupt was handled, a printk
call again will make it re-entries, or a swap might be happens.

- Not do prink in the interrupt context, and lock the scheduler during the EFI call.
samples/philosophers/
tests/kernel/interrupt/
tests/kernel/semaphore/sys_sem/
samples/kernel/metairq_dispatch/

- No tracing during switch in/out when using EFI console:
samples/subsys/tracing/

Fixes: #45929

comments:
According to description, on up_squared, when CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE is unset (use the EFI console only), in this test_posix_rw_lock() test case, it will stuck in the scheduler during the usleep(1000ns) call. If we change all the to usleep < 999us (That means k_busy_wait 999us)  or just simply use k_yield() instead of all usleep(). It won't stuck.

So far I have no idea why unset the CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE will lead usleep to hang up in scheduler.  Hi @andyross , @dcpleung , could you please give some suggestion of what direction I can dive in? Thank you!

Hi @andyross , could you please help to look at this issue when you got a chance?  Thank you!

We found not only this testcase failed when removing CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE=y on up_squared, but also Following testcases also failed due to this: 
tests/kernel/interrupt/arch.interrupt.x86_64
tests/kernel/semaphore/sys_sem/kernel.semaphore.usage
tests/subsys/logging/log_core_additional/logging.add.log1_user
tests/benchmarks/sys_kernel/benchmark.kernel.core

It's kind of a problem that an IRQ lock / unlock do not work in pair some where, but I am not sure.

In fact there's a known glitch with interrupts with the EFI console code on up_squared, see comments at: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/arch/x86/core/efi.c#L76 .  The short version is that the firmware enables interrupts while in the console output code somewhere, which means that if you try to log something while holding an IRQ lock, the firmware will break your lock.

This seems very unlikely to be a problem with general code (the window is very small), but I wouldn't be surprised if we had code in the test suite that exercised this reliably.  If so, the only really robust workaround is to disable the EFI console for those use cases.  The EFI layer is really intended just for system bringup and debugging (because it works everywhere and doesn't require figuring out a UART driver configuration).  It's never going to be as good as a proper hardware driver for logging output.

Some other things might be worth trying though:

* Disable core interrupts at the IO-APIC level (won't work for MSI)
* Detect the case where we're trying to make an EFI call inside an ISR that interrupted an existing EFI thunk.  The only way to recover this would be to abort the log, but it might be good enough to make tests pass.
* Rework the tests a tiny bit so that they don't hit interrupt conditions inside of EFI calls (most likely, what's happening is that the test has latched an interrupt with a lock held, so when it gets released the interrupt happens synchronously).
Thanks very much!  @andyross , I am trying your suggested solution.....
I'm going to remove myself as an assignee here, since I just turned in the hardware I'd need to reproduce this.  Please continue to ping me with questions, though!

Thanks @andyross , So far, there are 2 kinds of errors I can see:
(1) Like @andyross mentioned, the EFl simple text output call return with interrupt enable. we can workaround it by avoiding invoking printk() in the interrupt context.
(2) In some scenario, the k_sem_take() will be hang up. Not sure are these having the same root cause with the previous one.

Summary the current issues when CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE is unset:

1. **use printk in ISR context**
tests/kernel/interrupt/     => print in kernel_isr

2. **stuck at k_sleep or k_sem_take ( actually in z_pend_curr())** 
tests/posix/common/	     => u_sleep hang up
tests/kernel/semaphore/sys_sem/		=> k_msleep hang up after ztest error hook.
samples/subsys/portability/cmsis_rtos_v1/philosophers/ =>  stuck at  k_sem_take()    
samples/kernel/metairq_dispatch/ => stuck at k_msgq_get() (in z_pend_curr)

3. **Pass when CONFIG_SMP**
tests/kernel/mutex/sys_mutex/  => stuck at z_smp_init() due to it cannot get the start_flag = 1
samples/subsys/tracing/   => stuck at z_mem_manage_boot_finish when having userspace  (samples/subsys/tracing/tracing.user) 

4. **Need to implement logging backend for EFI console at least**        
tests/subsys/logging/log_core_additional/    (logging.add.log1_user)
samples/subsys/logging/logger/ (samples/subsys/logging/logger/sample.logger.basic)
samples/subsys/logging/syst/


5.  **printf() has no output , fixed by specifying efi_console_putchar as __stdout_hook**
tests/benchmarks/sys_kernel/  =>   (benchmark.kernel.core)
samples/application_development/external_lib/  
samples/posix/eventfd/    => printf has no output
samples/userspace/hello_world_user/  => printf has no output 

So, I would like to apply a solution:
For 1,2,3 we still keep the CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE=y
For 4 also keep CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE=y until a logging backend for EFI console has implemented. 
For 5 we can solve it now.

Excuse me, @andyross,  For 2 and 3,  I have tried several way but I cannot have a good fix on it. Such as check a interrupt status or store the RFLAG after the efi_call, etc. It seems like your "cli" solution is the best so far, but still has issue on 1, 2, 3.   Any further suggestion on this issue?

Do you have specifics on which tests fail?  It's likely to be specific tests that (1) do something while in a masked context that latches an interrupt and (2) do a printk(), which releases the interrupt lock and allows the interrupt to happen early.  Then later on something else happens that gets confused by the resulting corrupt state.  In those situations, I think the only reasonable workaround is just "don't use the EFI console" (though it might be possible to remove the offending printk).

It's a very useful feature, but that interrupt masking problem is going to make EFI logging unreliable.  There will be use cases where we just can't have it.

Thanks for the help! @andyross . Yes, I believe the 2 points you mentioned are what cause these.
And here are more testing information FYI:
